description: Do not sit near a window. Always keep documents together. Never tell anyone how much you earn. Never be the last one out. These persist in households in safe countries for two generations.

aspect: The silence is more transmissible than the story
description: Families that never discuss it produce children who know something enormous happened and have no shape for it, which is worse than the facts would have been.
energy_note: Growing up around an unlabelled thing.

aspect: Hypervigilance is taught by demonstration, not instruction
description: A parent who scans a restaurant on entry produces a child who scans a restaurant on entry. No one says anything and the behaviour transfers completely.
energy_note: Learned without a single word about it.

aspect: Achievement pressure as a war artefact
description: Everything was lost once; the only unloseable asset is a qualification in your head. So the child is pushed hard, for a reason grounded in a specific historical event they were not present at.
energy_note: Pushed by something that happened before you.

aspect: The protective factors are also transmitted
description: Family cohesion, ritual, humour and a coherent narrative of what happened are all documented buffers. The families that talk about it produce measurably better outcomes than the ones that do not.
energy_note: Talking about it is the intervention.
